title: Mixtape and Semester
premise: Edmund Eastwick transfers to Hollow Creek High for his final semester, counting down 118 days until graduation, when a history teacher pairs him with Priya Anand — his instant nemesis — to document the school's buried past. Their research uncovers that the school was built over a shuttered orphanage whose last residents vanished in 1974, and the pair begin hearing a mixtape of songs that shouldn't exist, each track marking someone else's disappearance. As Edmund and Priya's rivalry thaws into something like family, they realize the school 'keeps' students who learn too much, and Edmund is next on its list unless they tell the whole truth publicly. In the end, exposing the orphanage's records at graduation costs them their safe anonymity and nearly their friendship, but it frees the lost children — and gives both of them the belonging they'd stopped believing they deserved.
about_author: Yara Delacroix grew up in a mill town where the high school sat on land nobody would talk about, an experience that taught her how places hold grudges. She writes stories about stubborn teenagers who choose each other over safety.

chapters.title: One Hundred Eighteen Days
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He arrives at Hollow Creek High mid-year, mapping exits instead of hallways, determined to stay invisible until graduation. A hostile first collision with Priya Anand in the parking lot sets the tone: two survivors who mistake each other for threats. Beat: armored loneliness.

chapters.title: Assigned
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Mr. Okafor announces the semester capstone and pairs Edmund with Priya over both their objections. Forced to share a library table, they negotiate rules of engagement like rival nations signing a truce. Beat: reluctant proximity, sparks of grudging respect.

chapters.title: The Basement Nobody Mops
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Chasing a citation, Edmund finds a bricked archway behind the boiler room and a child's shoe fossilized in dust. He tells no one, but can't stop thinking about it. Beat: first crack in his indifference; curiosity as danger.

chapters.title: Ground Rules
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya lays out a contract for their partnership; Edmund counters by showing her the shoe photo. Her family has lived in Hollow Creek for generations, and her grandmother goes quiet at the word 'orphanage.' Beat: uneasy alliance formed over shared secrets.

chapters.title: Track One
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Alone after hours, Edmund hears faint music from the basement — a 1970s song he later finds on a cassette labeled only 'for the ones who stayed.' He pockets the tape against every instinct. Beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Silence
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya presses her grandmother, who reveals the St. Ambrose Home for Children closed overnight in 1974, its residents scattered or 'transferred,' records sealed. She begs Priya to drop the project. Beat: inherited fear; the past reaching through family.

chapters.title: Nemesis, Reluctantly
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. A late-night research session turns from bickering to honesty: Edmund admits he's bounced through six schools since his mother left; Priya confesses she performs perfection to keep her family's grief invisible. Beat: the rivalry breaks open into real friendship.

chapters.title: The Yearbook With Faces Missing
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. They find a 1974 yearbook where seven student photos have been scraped away. Cross-referencing names, they discover all seven were St. Ambrose kids enrolled here when it closed. Beat: the abstract becomes specific; seven missing children with faces.

chapters.title: Track Four
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The mixtape now plays songs Edmund never recorded onto it. When he plays Track Four aloud, the lights die floor-wide and a voice hums along. Priya witnesses it too. Beat: denial becomes impossible; the haunting is shared now.

chapters.title: Okafor Knows Something
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Mr. Okafor quietly returns their draft with one note: 'Stop asking about St. Ambrose.' Confronted, he admits a former partner teacher vanished in 1998 after researching the same thing. Beat: betrayal by an adult; the stakes turn personal and institutional.

chapters.title: Counting Wrong
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund's countdown notebook shows 118 days crossed off — but there are 119 marks. Someone, or something, is adding days he doesn't remember living. Beat: psychological unraveling; time itself becomes untrustworthy.

chapters.title: The Ones Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Following the tape's label, they find a hidden dormitory corridor behind the gym wall: small beds, drawings, and a ledger listing the seven children as 'retained.' Beat: horror and heartbreak fused; the school didn't lose them, it kept them.

chapters.title: What Friendship Costs
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya wants to go public immediately; Edmund, terrified of attention and of losing his one friend, wants to bury it. Their worst fight yet ends with Priya walking out. Beat: the theme made flesh — truth versus survival, and love caught between.

chapters.title: Alone With the Tape
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Working solo, Edmund plays the final blank side of the cassette and hears the children's voices asking him to say their names. He realizes the school is preparing to 'retain' him — his extra day already spent. Beat: terror transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Apology That Isn't Enough
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund finds Priya and apologizes without excuses, offering to go public even though it terrifies him. Priya doesn't forgive him instantly; she makes him prove it. Beat: repair begun honestly; friendship rebuilt on terms, not comfort.

chapters.title: Sealed Records
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Breaking into the county archive, they steal the sealed St. Ambrose files — and find a 1975 memo signed by the school's founding board authorizing the 'retention' to protect the institution. Beat: the villain revealed as ordinary complicity; rage as fuel.

chapters.title: They Start Taking Days
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Students who helped them begin forgetting Edmund exists; his locker empties; teachers skip his name in roll call. The school is erasing him ahead of schedule. Beat: rising dread; the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Graduation Eve
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. With the ceremony tomorrow, they plan to hijack the stage and read the seven names aloud. Okafor, choosing courage late, agrees to unlock the sound system. Beat: calm before the storm; found family assembled and committed.

chapters.title: The Longest Track
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The night before graduation, the school pulls Edmund into the retained corridor, trapping him among the children's rooms while the mixtape plays every track at once. Priya follows the music in and holds his hand, anchoring him. Beat: climax begins; love as lifeline.

chapters.title: Say Our Names
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. At commencement, mid-anthem, Priya seizes the microphone and reads the seven names while Edmund plays the tape over the speakers. The auditorium shudders; the bricked archway cracks open with light. Beat: climax — truth spoken publicly at maximum cost.

chapters.title: After the Applause
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The seven children walk out through the crowd, seen by everyone, then gone. The school board implodes; Okafor testifies; Edmund's erased days return. Some classmates resent them; neither cares. Beat: resolution — survival redefined as being witnessed.

chapters.title: Day Zero
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Graduation day proper: Edmund crosses the stage not counting days but keeping them, the mixtape's last side finally silent. He and Priya trade a burned copy labeled 'for the ones who left.' Beat: belonging earned; the sentence served and commuted.
